postings.title: Internships
strengths: Direct exposure to U.S. foreign policy and diplomacy at the committee level, precisely aligned with your core interest area.
Access to congressional staff, committee members, and foreign policy networks that will be invaluable for your legislative/cabinet-advisory career path.

Resume credential that signals serious policy intent and will strengthen applications to think tanks, executive-branch roles, and graduate programs.
weaknesses: Highly competitive for sophomores; SFRC typically prioritizes juniors/seniors or students with prior Hill experience.

It also positions you to explore how Congress handles S&T diplomacy and technology governance—core pillars of your long-term agenda.
postings.difficulty: Moderately difficult for a sophomore; SFRC is prestigious and draws strong applicants, but your GPA, Batten track record, and clear articulated interest in foreign policy will help you stand out if you secure a personal referral or reach out directly to your Virginia senator's office.
postings.approach: Contact both your home-state senators' offices (Virginia) directly—ask their chief of staff or foreign policy staffer if they have summer internship slots or can refer you to SFRC. Emphasize your Batten enrollment and specific interest in S&T diplomacy or defense policy. Apply through official channels as well, but a warm introduction will dramatically improve your odds.
